thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: Elevated queue depth and degraded tail latency for tenant 'orpheus' (dedicated-us-west-2 pool). Alert threshold: queue_depth > 200 for 3m. Current queue_depth=1187, p99 latency 2.1s. Paging oncall.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Posting initial triage. Which nodes are hot? Any obvious cascade from other tenants?
maria-ng: I'm looking — orpheus traffic spike looks sudden, mostly multi-turn chat completions. I see continuous 1k TPS equivalent of small requests, but tails ASH shows large batches building up on scheduler.
jamal: Confirmed dedicated pool saturation on g4dn-8x. Scheduler logs show repeated batching failures and long waiting windows. Possible max_batch_tokens overflow. grabbing logs.
sean-l: @maria-ng can you dump scheduler metrics? I want active_batches, queued_tokens, max_batch_tokens per tenant.
maria-ng: metrics snapshot:
```
tenant: orpheus
active_batches: 82
queued_requests: 1143
queued_tokens: 498000
max_batch_tokens_global: 65536
tenant_max_batch_tokens: 8192  # currently overridden for orpheus
avg_batch_size_tokens: 512
batch_wait_ms_p90: 420
```
jamal: whoa queued_tokens huge. Looks like many small requests accumulating; scheduler keeps waiting to fill to tenant_max_batch_tokens (8192) before dispatch decisions cause head-of-line blocking.
oncall-sre: TL;DR: tenant-level max_batch_tokens is too high relative to their request size distribution. We should lower tenant_max_batch_tokens and enable rapid eviction/shaper to push throughput. Rolling change plan:
  1) Apply emergency config change to tenant override: set tenant_max_batch_tokens = 2048
  2) Enable tenant_queue_shaper (burst_shed = true, cooldown_ms = 250)
  3) Monitor queue depth & p99 for 5m, rollback if errors spike
  4) Customer-facing note through @customer-success
eng-runtime: Agree. Lowering will increase number of batches but reduce waiting time and queued_tokens. Also add quick KV-cache bypass for small requests if needed.
ops-liaison: Heads-up: changing tenant_max_batch_tokens is safe for dedicated pool but will temporarily increase GPU overhead. We have capacity headroom of ~12% across pool.
oncall-sre: I'll do the change via config map patch. Applying now:
```
kubectl -n redwood patches config tenant-overrides/orpheus --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/tenant_max_batch_tokens","value":"2048"},{"op":"replace","path":"/data/tenant_queue_shaper","value":"{\"burst_shed\":true,\"cooldown_ms\":250}"}]'
```
incident-bot: deploy-bot: configpatch/tenant-overrides/orpheus succeeded (commit: 7b3e2a9). Rolling restart not needed; scheduler picks up overrides live.
maria-ng: change observed: tenant_max_batch_tokens now 2048. Immediate queue effect: queued_tokens -> 240k (within 45s). active_batches -> 160 (more batches), avg_batch_size_tokens -> 320. p99 latency dropped to 1.1s.
oncall-sre: Nice. Keep monitoring for 10m. If queue_depth stops decreasing, we will enable max_concurrent_batches=4 for tenant.
jamal: quick note — some client errors spiking (HTTP 429) around the time of change, likely due to reshuffling. Details:
```
[2026-03-15T22:03:01Z] tenant=orpheus code=429 route=/v1/generate client=orpheus-app err=rate_limit_exceeded
count: 18 over 30s
```
sean-l: 429s are acceptable transiently; we'll inform customer. As long as p99 improves and error rate goes <0.5% after 5m, we keep.
oncall-sre: Customer comms draft (for @customer-success):
"Hi Orpheus engineering — we saw a sudden traffic profile that caused batching to accumulate and increase tail latency. We applied a temporary scheduler config to reduce per-tenant max_batch_tokens and enabled burst shedding. This should reduce latency; you might see a small uptick in throughput cost. We're monitoring and can revert/change knobs if you prefer a different tradeoff."
customer-success: I'll send that. Also offering options: longer term we can propose adaptive knob that follows request token distribution.
eng-runtime: Noted: we should also add a guard to auto-lower tenant_max_batch_tokens when queued_tokens > 200k for >60s. Filing quick follow-up ticket.
oncall-sre: Update at +5m: queue_depth=220 (down from 1143), queued_tokens=90k, p99=0.95s, overall errors tapered to 3 x 429s in 5m window (~0.03%).
ops-liaison: Pool GPU utilization rose to 88% after change (was 76%). Still within burst headroom.
jamal: lifting a small concern: some internal batch assembly logs show `batch_drop: true` for very large requests ( > 2500 tokens ). We might need to set max_single_request_tokens for tenant to 4000 to avoid drops.
oncall-sre: Good catch. We'll set `tenant_max_single_request_tokens=4000` now to prevent drops. Patching:
```
kubectl -n redwood patches config tenant-overrides/orpheus --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/tenant_max_single_request_tokens","value":"4000"}]'
```
incident-bot: deploy-bot: configpatch/tenant-overrides/orpheus succeeded (commit: 7b3e2b0).
maria-ng: Applied. No more batch_drop logs seen in tail for the last minute.
oncall-sre: After 12m: metrics stable. Final snapshot:
```
queue_depth: 136
queued_tokens: 74k
p99 latency: 0.88s
active_batches: 148
gpu_util: 84%
error_rate_5m: 0.02% (mostly transient 429s)
```
oncall-sre: Mitigation complete. Next steps:
 - Keep tenant_max_batch_tokens = 2048 as baseline for next 24h
 - Build adaptive rule to auto-downscale tenant_max_batch_tokens when queued_tokens spike
 - Postmortem to include customer traffic pattern, suggested client-side guidance (smaller requests, batching hints), and proposed adaptive feature
 - @eng-runtime to file follow-up ticket for auto-guard
maria-ng: I'll record logs & graphs in the incident board and keep monitoring overnight.
customer-success: Message sent to Orpheus: shared mitigation details + offer to sync. They replied "thanks, saw latency drop, can we review traffic shaping options".
oncall-sre: Closing thread, marking as handoff -> followup ticket created: R-INC-20260315-orpheus-bespoke-batch. Assigning to eng-runtime and product.
eng-runtime: Acknowledged. Will pick up adaptive rule and follow up with product for tenant controls UX.
incident-bot: Incident closed (manual) — severity: S2, duration: 00:18:26. Logs archived to /incidents/2026-03-15/orpheus-bespoke-batch.log :thumbsup:
